item.title: No. 7 Texas thumps Grambling State, 93-62
item.description: AUSTIN — In another businesslike performance by the No. 7 Texas Longhorns to start the season, head coach Sean Miller’s team took control early and didn’t allow much rhythm to the Grambling State Tigers until late in the contest at the Moody Center on Monday in a 93-62 victory. A big second half propelled junior center Matas Vokietaitis to a game-high 26 points on 8-of-12 shooting from the floor and 10-of-12 shooting from the free-throw line, including 15 points after halftime as the big Lithuanian hit all four of his shot attempts and all seven of his free throws, adding four rebounds. The story of the first half was freshman guard Joe Sterling, who notched 13 points on 4-of-5 shooting overall, 3-of-4 shooting from three, and 2-of-3 shooting from the line with two assists and two steals, continuing the strong start to his Longhorns career after getting overlooked by high-major programs during his recruitment. Freshman forward Marcus Spears Jr. (12 points), junior wing Elyjah Freeman (11 points), and junior forward David Punch (10 points) also reached double figures as the Longhorns shot 50.8 percent from the floor, but struggled times at the free-throw line in shooting 64.3 percent. Texas notched a 14-0 advantage in fast-break points, a 46-18 edge in points in the paint, and the Longhorns off the bench outscored the Tigers 41-26. A high-low action on the first possession produced an entry pass to Vokietaitis and a foul against Grambling State seven-footer Isaiah Miranda. After freshman guard Austin Goosby turned a steal by Punch into a transition slam by Freeman, the Auburn transfer drew a second foul on Miranda on a drive to the basket. Miranda stayed in the game, missing his first two shots, but in the wake of the Tigers scoring their points on a corner three, Vokietaitis recovered his own miss and drew a third whistle against Miranda, sending him to the bench at the 16:57 mark. The concern for Longhorns head coach Sean Miller was 4-of-9 start at the free-throw line, but the team’s defense was stifling, heading into the first media break with a 10-3 lead. A set play for Vokietaitis drew the sixth foul against the Tigers a little more than four minutes into the game, the seventh came 40 seconds later, and the eighth 45 seconds after that, coming on a three-point attempt by Sterling, who missed another attempt this season after shooting almost 99 percent during the team’s offseason program. item.title: McGonigle, Stewart win ROY Awards
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27, 2026: Kevin McGonigle #7 of the Detroit Tigers celebrates with teammates as he exits the game during the eighth inning against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by George Kubas/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Kevin McGonigle of the Detroit Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Cincinnati Reds have been named the winners of the American League and National League Rookie of the Year Awards, respectively. McGonigle led the American League with 7.1 bWAR this season, slashing .278/.376/.430 while splitting his time between shortstop and third base. He received 28 first place votes and two second place votes. Cleveland Guardians starting pitcher Parker Messick came in second and received the other two first place votes, along with 25 second place votes, two third place votes and a fourth place vote. Payton Tolle, Munetaka Murakami and Chase DeLauter rounded out the top five. There were thirteen players in all who received votes, with the Guardians and White Sox having three apiece. No Texas Rangers rookies received votes, which makes sense when you recall Peyton Gray won the team Rookie of the Year Award. Texas has had two A.L. ROY winners in its history — Neftali Feliz in 2010 and Mike Hargrove in 1974. The full ballots and results for the American League voting can be found here. Stewart received 20 first place votes, with second place finisher Carson Benge and third place finisher JJ Wetherholt receiving seven and three first place votes, respectively. Nolan McLean finished fourth, and TJ Rumfield finished fifth. Texas has never had an N.L. ROY winner in its history. The full ballots and results for the National League voting can be found here.

item.title: Evan Roberts, Tiki Barber rip Fox broadcasters over ‘terrible’ Malik Nabers commentary: ‘They made that up’
item.description: Credit: Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images, WFAN New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers was quite emotive during Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles, and Fox’s broadcasting booth took notice. As the game wore on, Nabers appeared to grow frustrated as the Giants struggled to get him the ball and later, after he dropped a touchdown pass. Fox analyst Greg Olsen and play-by-play partner Joe Davis discussed Nabers’ body language after he was seen slamming his helmet following a frustrating fourth-quarter sequence. “His body language has been terrible today,” Davis said. Later, after Davis brought up Nabers’ body language when the wide receiver appeared frustrated after a teammate scored a go-ahead touchdown, Olsen offered commentary about the wideout’s state of mind . “I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot really good players. There’s never been a great wide receiver who hasn’t demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory,” Olsen said. “But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That’s great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can’t still be worried about your targets. That’s the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You’ve just got to keep it in check.” The Giants won the game, but Davis and Olsen’s commentary about Nabers was a hot topic in the New York sports media scene, especially after Nabers took to social media and, incorrectly, accused Olsen of calling him a bad teammate. The New York Post also wrote a story that initially misattributed quotes to the Fox analyst about Nabers. That prompted a response from Olsen, who shared his comments on X , adding, “At no point did we ever say he was a bad teammate.” That still wasn’t enough for WFAN’s Evan Roberts and Tiki Barber, who lashed out at both Davis and Olsen over their commentary and the perception that they thought Nabers was a bad teammate. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Evric Gray
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Evric Gray. An alum of UNLV, he went unselected in the 1993 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the (then) New Jersey (now, Brooklyn) Nets in 1996. The Bloomington, California native played the sole season of his NBA career with New Jersey, leaving the league as a player afterward. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Gray put up 2.6 points per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Can the Rams really add a receiver to replace Puka Nacua?
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for at least four weeks , and with the NFL trade deadline less that 24-hours away, should the Rams make a big-time trade for a wide receiver? Whether they do or not, there is no replacing Nacua, who’s carried the offensive passing game since the Rams lost Davante Adams, who’s also on IR. If the Rams could make a blockbuster (or any) trade to save 2026, they would, but that may not be an option as the NFL trade period comes to its close. The Rams may choose to go with the group they have, injuries and all, and if they do, then they’ll need to play better. Change for the sake of change doesn’t guarantee success. Though it could be naive of McVay to not make major changes on offense this season, the group of pass catchers we’ve seen may be the group going forward until guys get healthy, unless something changes, that appears to be the case. Who could the Rams add at receiver? L.A. has been rumored or speculated as linked to potentially trading for receivers like Josh Downs , Brian Thomas Jr. Stefon Diggs , George Pickens and more. Would any of these receivers do what Nacua does for L.A.’s offense? The run after catch, the physicality, maybe. The relationship he’s s built with Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and the offense? Can any of the names above fill in well enough for both Nacua and Adams to make a trade worthwhile? The Rams would have to make the trade to find out. Can the Rams trade for a receiver who boosts the offense? Yes. They could also trade for a receiver who struggles to connect and build chemistry with Stafford as L.A.’s veteran quarterback is struggling currently with receivers like Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Players Stafford has worked with for years. Trading for a receiver like Thomas Jr. is splashy, but would he and Stafford work well together? Does he fit McVay’s scheme? Would a player like Pickens fit McVay’s culture? Are those receivers worth the Rams sending draft capital for? A trade does not guarantee the Rams a playoff spot Are there any receivers available for the Rams to get going into Week 10 that truly increase their odds at a playoff spot? Going into their 10th game of the year, the Rams sit at 9th in the NFC playoff picture , below the Seattle Seahawks. Below the entire NFC North. Well below the 49ers who sit atop the NFC. Injury is playing a role in the Rams struggles, but so is inconsistent offensive play and coaching. The defense for L.A. has overcome missing Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Aaron Donald, Nate Landman and more, but the defense for the Rams has been objectively better than their offense this year. item.title: Rams' Puka Nacua likely headed to injured reserve with knee injury, turf toe
item.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) during Rams training camp at the Loyola Marymount University on Monday, July 27th in Westchester, CA. WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least a month after he suffered sprains to the MCL and PCL in his right knee, along with turf toe, during Sunday's 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders. Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that Nacua will likely be placed on injured reserve, dealing another significant blow to a Los Angeles offense already missing several key contributors, including wide receiver Davante Adams. "As far as Puka Nacua, he suffered an MCL/PCL sprain and also turf toe," McVay said. "He's going to be out for a good amount of time. He will probably be a guy that we'll put on IR as a result of that." McVay declined to establish a definitive timetable for Nacua's return but acknowledged that the receiver is expected to miss at least four weeks. "I'm reluctant to put too much of a timetable, but I would say there's a strong chance that we put him on IR," McVay said. "We're thinking it's going to be at least a month." Nacua suffered the injury on a jet sweep late in Sunday's game when he absorbed a hard hit to his right knee. McVay said he immediately feared something was wrong after watching the collision. "I saw the way that he got hit on the last jet sweep that we ran," McVay said. "He got up and came off, but the way that he took a shot just from that guy inside out, it looked like there could have been something there. He's as tough as it gets and he was able to get off, but I was concerned about that." The injury was particularly devastating considering Nacua's performance against Washington. McVay said the receiver caught 14 of 19 targets Sunday, continuing to establish himself as one of the NFL's most productive offensive weapons. McVay also acknowledged second-guessing his decision to call the play that resulted in the injury, questioning whether he could have protected Nacua from the violent collision. "I'd be lying to you if I said I haven't questioned the decision making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion and maybe end of the game that would have led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee," McVay said. "It's stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we have to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine." McVay said the Rams have previously discussed ways Nacua could avoid unnecessary contact, including running out of bounds rather than fighting for additional yards. However, he acknowledged that the receiver's physical playing style is part of what makes him special. item.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports The NBA is bringing the All-Star Game back to Miami. The league plans to name the Miami Heat as the official host for the 2028 event. This news marks a major shift for the franchise. The city has not hosted the midseason showcase since 1990. That was nearly four decades ago. The decision changes how the team plans its schedule and community events. Fans can expect a full weekend of basketball action right here in town. League officials have reached a deal with the Heat. The announcement is set for November 30, according to a person with knowledge of the matter who spoke to The Associated Press. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver and Heat chairman Micky Arison are expected to attend the press event. The logo for the weekend has already been approved. Most of the logistical planning is well underway. This is not a vague idea; the work is happening now. Why the Long Wait for Miami The delay in hosting the event was not about a lack of interest. Since launching in 1988, the Heat have hosted the All-Star game just once. The main reason was a conflict with the Miami International Boat Show. According to Anthony Chiang of The Miami Herald, the boat show typically occurs during Presidents’ Day weekend. This is the same time the NBA schedules its big weekend. There was not enough hotel and event space to hold both events at once. That problem is finally solved. Chiang reports that the boat show will move to a different weekend in 2028. This change opened the door for Miami to host the league’s biggest party. Chiang reports that the league contacted the team regarding hosting the event. The Heat did not have to chase this opportunity. The timing simply worked out for the first time in a long while. Where the Action Will Happen The main games will take place at the team’s home court. Expect All-Star Saturday night and the Sunday game to be held at the Kaseya Center. Per Hoops Rumors , the specific dates are likely February 19 and February 20. Other parts of the weekend will spread out across the city. Events like Rising Stars and the G League Up Next Game will move to the Miami Beach Convention Center and the Watsco Center on the University of Miami campus. Using multiple arenas is a common move for All-Star weekends. This season’s events in Phoenix will use more than one spot as well. The 2028 event fits into a rotation of host cities. This weekend gives them a chance to show off their basketball culture. There is a special angle for LeBron James. Last offseason, he agreed to a two-year deal with Philadelphia. item.title: Four-star WR Anthony Roberts flips from Virginia Tech to Wake Forest
item.description: Rolesville (NC) High Rivals four-star receiver Anthony Roberts has flipped his commitment from Virginia Tech to Wake Forest. He was on campus this weekend for a visit that included the Demon Deacons game against Merrimack. Ranked by Rivals as the No. 43 receiver in the country and No. 12 player in the state, Roberts had been a verbal to the Hokies since April. Now he’s excited to be a pledge to Wake Forest. “I just feel the coaching staff, my relationship with all the coaches there, I feel throughout the whole process they haven’t showed me nothing but greatness and building that connection made them feel right for me,” Roberts said. The 6-foot-2, 190-pound Roberts is having a terrific senior season averaging over 26 yards per reception, catching 26 passes for 653 yards and 12 touchdowns. He loves the trajectory of the program at Wake Forest under head coach Jake Dickert. “All the time and effort they put into the program is coming together. Just as it was at his previous school, he showed he can win there and at Wake Forest they showed they can win.” Future position coach Dyrell Roberts has led the charge in recruiting Roberts and the two have a great connection. “It’s not too far from home,” Roberts said. “The best in North Carolina stay in North Carolina and I want to stay there and put on for the state of North Carolina. Another thing I would say is my relationship with Coach Roberts has been there since he’s been at ECU. He offered me at ECU and went to Wake Forest and we’ve been locked in ever since.” Now Roberts is locked in with Wake Forest. He is now one of the jewels of this 2027 Demon Deacons class. item.title: Mariners hire hitting coach, bench coach for 2027 season
item.description: Mariners hire new bench and hitting coaches for 2027 season Courtesy: Seattle Mariners Less than a week after introducing their new manager , the Mariners are adding two more members to their coaching staff. The Mariners announced Monday that they have brought on both Tanner Swanson and CJ Gillman to assist new manager Jason Kanzler. Swanson, who spent seven years with the New York Yankees, will serve as the Mariners bench coach for the 2027 season. Gillman, on the other hand, will be the Mariners’ next hitting coach. Gillman spent last year with the Washington Nationals, acting as their director of hitting. “I am excited to have Tanner and CJ join our coaching staff,” Mariners Manager Jason Kanzler wrote in a press release. “Both individuals bring an exceptional understanding of the game and skillsets that I am confident will help maximize the talent on our roster.” Despite Swanson and Gillman spending the previous year with teams across the country, both have ties to Washington state. Swanson spent his years growing up in Roslyn. He then went to school at Cle Elum-Roslyn High School and Central Washington University, according to the Mariners. Gillman rejoins the Mariners, after first becoming their minor league hitting coordinator in 2022. Gillman stayed in that position until 2025.

item.description: Rich Clark, College Football Playoff executive director, was in town around this time last year to announce that Tampa Bay would host the CFP National Championship on Jan. 22, 2029. ©Jefferee Woo Once upon a time, they told us tradition mattered. (It didn’t.) Around the same time, they said college football’s regular season was sacred. (It wasn’t.) Those same bigshots said they had a duty to protect the schedule of student-athletes. (Not so much.) So now, after decades of fighting the tide on a college football playoff, the sport’s architects have journeyed to the opposite extreme. ESPN (you’ll understand why later) broke the story Monday morning that college football will be moving to a 24-team playoff as soon as next season. That means 30 years ago we were still operating under an archaic bowl system that few loved other than college administrators. Once they saw the light, we were given a two-team playoff (the Bowl Championship Series in 1998), which expanded to a four-team postseason (the College Football Playoff in 2014) and then a 12-team playoff (in 2024), and now we have a 24-team playoff beginning in roughly nine months. That’s not an evolution, that’s a mutation. They said they did it so more teams had a chance to win but, of course that’s rubbish. They did it for the cash. And now we’re in a position where a lot of the fans who were once clamoring for a playoff system are now distressed that college football bears little resemblance to the sport they once loved. Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza holds the trophy after the Hoosiers' win against Miami in the College Football Playoff National Championship game this past January in Miami Gardens. “We’re aware of the fan sentiment and that many fans aren’t in favor of expansion,” CFP executive director Rich Clark said in a conference call on Monday. “That was certainly weighed into the decision. It was considered. Ultimately, we just need to make a spectacular playoff. “I mean, the CFP has a responsibility to our fans, they’re the lifeblood of college football. We owe it to them to make this great. That really is our intent. We appreciate our fans. We did take into account their sentiment. That was rolled into this decision. item.description: The Grand Valley State men's basketball team survived a last-second thriller to beat Northwood 80-79 on Monday, Nov. 9, in Midland. The Lakers were poor from the free-throw line, making just 9-of-17. Austin Tory led GVSU with 18 points, seven rebounds, three blocks and a steal. He was 9-for-15 from the field. Dylan Smith had a double-double with 11 points and 10 rebounds. The Lakers got strong bench play with Antaune Allen netting 15 points and five rebounds and Miles Sidney chipped in 10 points.
